text:
liam: quick dump of the GPTQ hybrid bake results across Llama2-13B / Mistral-7B / Qwen-7B. sweep included GPTQ-4, AWQ-4, INT8-opt probes and an FP8 baseline. TL;DR: Mistral gives the best throughput <-> quality tradeoff at GPTQ-4 with our kv-align patch; Qwen drops on long-context numeric tasks; Llama2 is the safest for instruction fidelity with smallest accuracy delta.

maya: nice, can you paste the top-line numbers?

liam: sure — high level (Δ = change vs FP16 baseline):
- Mistral-7B GPTQ-4: latency -42%, throughput +2.3x, MMLU Δ -0.9 pts, WinRate conv. eval Δ -1.1%
- Qwen-7B GPTQ-4: latency -38%, throughput +2.0x, MMLU Δ -2.8 pts, Numeric QA Δ -6.5% (long ctx)
- Llama2-13B GPTQ-4: latency -35%, throughput +1.9x, MMLU Δ -0.6 pts, Instr. acc Δ -0.8%
- AWQ-4 (mixed across families): latency -55% (short seq), throughput +2.8x, MMLU Δ -1.8 pts, but KV-cache hits are ~12% worse on sequences >2048
- INT8-opt: best stability on code tasks but slightly higher latency than GPTQ for batch sizes >8
- FP8 prototype: best density, but saw occasional >5% regression on instruction paraphrase sets (likely numeric instabilities)

kevin: curious about the eval suite — which suites and seeds?

liam: evals used: MMLU, GSM8K (math), SQuAD/QA dev, instruction-winrate harness (internal), codebench-lite. Seeds: standard 3-run aggregate for MMLU/GSM8K. Long-context probe: synthetic math-with-context up to 8192 tokens.

sara: what was the KV/cache misalignment you mentioned for AWQ? any root-cause?

liam: short answer: AWQ quant layout reorders some weight blocks; our runtime needed a small remap for KV projection ordering. Without the remap, older KV cache indices are shifted causing token drift over long contexts. Patch "kv-align-v2" fixes it (added to the bake pipeline).

bakebot: autopost: bake 4398765432 finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-bakes/4398765432/{mistral,qwen,llama2}-gptq-awq-int8-report.json. CI: passed smoke, 2/3 stability tests for FP8 (one flaky seed).

maya: liam — can you drop the command you ran? makes it easier to repro.

liam: pasted below:
```bash
bakebot run --suite hybrid-gptq-sweep \
  --models llama2-13b mistral-7b qwen-7b \
  --quant-schemes gptq4 awq4 int8 fp8-proto \
  --seq-lens 512,2048,8192 \
  --metrics mmlu,gsm8k,winrate,qa,codebench \
  --kv-patch kv-align-v2 \
  --out s3://redwood-bakes/4398765432
```

kevin: good. any notable decode-time memory regressions? GPTQ seemed fine in our perf env but AWQ sometimes used +200MB due to weight unpack buffer.

liam: yea noted — AWQ runtime currently unpacks a small chunk for each layer for fast int kernels; overhead ~150-250MB on 13B depending on seq len. GPTQ stays near FP16 device memory; FP8 reduced VRAM by ~30% but saw the earlier stability flake.

sara: which libs/versions? we should pin before rollout.

liam: gptq-lib v0.4.1 (our fork), awq v0.3.2, quant-tooling v2.1.0, runtime-gpu v5.6.2 (kernel fixes for kv-align-v2 included).

maya: recommendation for staging rollout?

liam: Proposed rollout plan:
- Canary: Mistral-7B GPTQ-4 on dedicated-small pool (2xA10) with 5% traffic, monitor winrate and QA pass @ 10k samples/day.
- If stable 48h: expand to 25% and enable batching optimizations.
- Qwen GPTQ-4: hold off on long-context customer workloads; enable only for short-session chat for now.
- AWQ: use for latency-sensitive short seq (<1024) customer tiers, but require kv-align-v2 runtime >=5.6.2.
- FP8: keep experimental flag, run nightly stability sweeps.

kevin: agree. let's also add automatic fallback to FP16-hosted model if winrate drops >3% in canary window.

liam: will add rollout policy in console: canary -> monitor(winrate,gsm8k) -> auto-fallback fp16-hosted.

maya: can you attach the short CSV of per-task deltas to the thread?

liam: attaching (artifacts link above). I'll also export a condensed csv to the eng-ml drive.

bakebot: note: regression alert suppressed for FP8 until we stabilize seed flakiness. use flag --ignore-known-fp8-flake to reproduce.

sara: thanks — this is actionable. i'll open a ticket to track kv-align runtime rollout and awq mem-opt.

liam: cheers. ping me if you want the raw logits or eval harness to run new seeds.
